```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 12
    n_vehicles = 4
    Q = 62  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[87, 45], [22, 81], [88, 67], [9, 11], [10, 45], [44, 10], [72, 47], [78, 72], [49, 32], [12, 42], [85, 88], [26, 81]]
    demands = [14, 17, 14, 8, 22, 7, 9, 17, 12, 13, 8, 25]
    time_windows = [[0, 323], [34, 128], [57, 125], [53, 119], [53, 144], [48, 101], [37, 134], [25, 110], [44, 111], [28, 92], [44, 117], [72, 152], [47, 130]]
    service_times = [11, 10, 6, 12, 14, 6, 15, 9, 11, 6, 6, 9]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Routing and Scheduling for Customer Deliveries

Overview
We operate a fleet of identical delivery vehicles from a single central depot. For the current planning horizon, we will dispatch vehicles at time 0 to serve the scheduled set of customer locations and require all deployed vehicles to return to the depot before the depot closes. Each vehicle will make one continuous trip: depart at time 0, visit its assigned sequence of customers, and return to the depot before the end of the day.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
Our task is to determine which customers each vehicle will serve and in what order, while setting arrival and service start times that respect each customer’s delivery window. Every customer must be visited exactly once. Travel time between any two locations is taken as the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with an implicit speed of 1 so that distance units and time units align. Using an additional vehicle reduces the length and complexity of individual routes but adds a fixed deployment cost, so we must balance route distance against vehicle usage.

Operational Requirements
- Departures and returns: All deployed vehicles leave the depot at time 0 and must return before the depot’s closing time. No mid-route returns or reloads are permitted.
- Customer coverage: Each customer must be served exactly once. Deliveries may not be split across vehicles.
- Time windows: Service must begin within the customer’s stated time window. If a vehicle arrives early, it must wait until the window opens. Late starts are not allowed.
- Service times: Each stop requires a defined unloading/service duration. After service completion, the vehicle departs immediately to the next location or to the depot.
- Capacity: Vehicles are capacity-constrained. The total demand assigned to any single route must not exceed the vehicle’s carrying capacity at any point in the trip.
- Travel times: Movement between the depot and customers, and between customers, follows straight-line distances based on their map coordinates. With speed set to 1, the distance traveled equals the time spent in transit.
- Cost structure: Total cost includes the sum of all route distances traveled across deployed vehicles plus a fixed deployment cost for each vehicle put into service.

Goal
Build a set of feasible routes—one per deployed vehicle—that:
- Visit every customer exactly once,
- Start all vehicles at time 0 and return them to the depot before closing,
- Respect each customer’s delivery window and service time (waiting if early),
- Keep the total load on any route within vehicle capacity,
- Minimize the combined cost of total travel distance and the fixed cost of the vehicles used.

Expected Output
- A route plan indicating which customers are assigned to each deployed vehicle and the visit order.
- Planned arrival and service start times at each customer, including any waiting time.
- Confirmation that every route respects capacity limits, all time windows, and the requirement to return to the depot before closing.
- A cost summary showing total distance traveled and vehicle deployment costs.
